speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked	the Minister for Education (Schools) (a) what is the progress on the setting up of school-based Student Care Centres (SCCs) in all primary schools; (b) whether the Ministry is seeing increasing demand for more places; and (c) whether the Ministry has plans to increase the number of places in each school.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: Student Care Centres (SSCs) play an important role with their after-school support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: The provision of school-based SCC places has largely kept pace with demand as the majority of the schools do not have waitlists.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: For the schools with a waitlist, the average number of students on a waitlist is less than 10.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: But having said that, I want to assure the Member that MOE will continue to monitor the demand for school-based SCC places and work with our schools to improve the accessibility of SCCs through the setting up of new SCCs as well as expanding capacity for existing ones, where appropriate, and also at a pace that does not compromise the quality of after-school care.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The enrolment numbers for SCCs increasing from 3,000 to 18,000 is a six-fold increase.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Parents I spoke to appreciate the SCC support as this makes their lives better as working parents.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I sense that the demand will continue to rise.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, I want to ask the Parliamentary Secretary whether MOE has plans to further scale up both the SCCs within the schools as well as those that are outside the schools.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Would MOE work with some of the voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) which are interested to set up SCCs, which they slowed or stopped since the school-based SCCs were introduced?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If MOE can increase the effort, that would really help parents, especially the working  parents.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank the Member, Mr Liang, for his supplementary questions and also sharing the observation and feedback from the residents.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We certainly agree that after-school care is a crucial period for influence and care where values and children's learning can be reinforced after school hours.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It is certainly MOE's priority to ensure that a nurturing environment is availed to the students who most need after-school care, where they can grow and flourish after school.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We appreciate the observation that is shared with us, arising from residents' feedback.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, 45% of the 147 centres are operated by VWOs and the remaining 55% of the centres are operated by private sector commercial operators.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I wish to assure Mr Liang and the House that the current rate of expansion meets demand.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We also recognise that demand may vary from school to school and from area to area.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We work very closely with the school principals who will know and would have a good pulse check on the demand for SCC places in the school arising from meetings with parents and parents' feedback.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In places of higher demand, MOE works closely with the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) as well as our SCC operators, be it the VWOs or the private sector operators, to increase capacity where were can.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I have shared two ways where we can increase capacity: one, opening up an SCC in each of the remaining primary schools – and that will be another 43 more – to cover the total number of 190 primary schools by the year 2020.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Another way we can inject capacity is to increase capacity in existing centres.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Certainly, the school will be happy to work with the operators to provide them more classrooms so that they can extend capacity, but it is not just the hardware; the software is also important.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We want to make sure that as we expand capacity, we are also not compromising the quality of care given to our students.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure Mr Liang that the two Ministries will continue to work closely to monitor the capacity as well as the demand for SCC places across school-based centres as well as community-based centres.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This is especially so for children who lack such a home environment after-school for various reasons.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We do that because we know that with after-school support, from schools and the community, more parents would be able to work with peace of mind knowing that their kids receive good care after school.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And to this end, we will be happy to work with Mr Liang to look at the needs of his constituency so that families and also students receive quality after-school care.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Does MOE play some role in reviewing the programmes that the SCCs run to level up in terms of the quality of their programmes and to share learnings as to the quality of the programmes?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My second question is on students with special needs.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Are teachers in at least some of these SCCs trained to provide the appropriate care for students with different types of special needs?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The MOE team works closely with the MSF team to support the Student Care Officers (SCOs) working in the SCC to provide care for the students after-school hours.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And we also work with them to provide professional development support.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: They already have SCCs in 15 schools to provide care for students who most need this.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: MOE, together with the self-help groups as well as the other operators, is also looking at how to facilitate sharing of best practices for the SCOs.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: To the Member's second question on special needs, based on the feedback from parents, they see a lot of benefits of having their children stay in an SCC in a school-based environment because it is within the school premises and this is where the principal or what we call the Allied Educator (AED) will be able to bridge the communications with the SCO with regard to the learning needs or learning difficulties of certain students in the SCCs and provide relevant support to them.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The support being given is not just support from the MOE side but also the relevant disability division in MSF.
